text:
ashley: Heads up — seeing a burst of preview-proxy logs making requests to 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ in the last 20m. sample: `GET /_preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` from pool-3 nodes. Not sure if SSRF or misconfigured prefetch.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2028-042 — preview-proxy possible SSRF to metadata service. Severity: P2. Paging @oncall.
jon: Confirmed. Multiple requests from preview-proxy instances (10.12.3.45, 10.12.3.47). I can isolate the nodes.
maria: I'm rolling an egress firewall rule to block 169.254.169.254 for preview-proxy subnets now. ETA ~2m.
devops-bot: Egress block applied to sg-pprod-frontend (us-east-1) via policy block-pproxy-metadata. change_id: ch_4521.
samir: Good call. Also plan to add host header validation on proxy and disable following redirects to internal IP ranges. Patching proxy config.
kevin: Quick check — do logs include any auth headers? I see some entries with `X-User-Auth: token_xyz` in upstream call logs (masked here). If tokens were forwarded we should rotate.
ashley: Starting API key rotation for preview-service in prod. KMS rotation request created: kms-rotate/preview-service-keys.
maria: Found one cached edge preview that pre-fetched the internal metadata earlier. Purging CDN cache for preview_id pv-8f3 now. Purge started.
jon: Running a sweep for outbound connections from preview-proxy to other private ranges (10.128.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8). So far only metadata IP observed.
samir: Action items (short):
  1) enforce host header allowlist + disable redirects to RFC1918/private ranges
  2) add per-tenant RBAC on proxy so preview requests cannot target internal hostnames
  3) add audit logging for every preview fetch (origin IP, host header, url hash)
  4) KMS-backed signed preview URLs to prevent arbitrary upstream fetches
I'll open the tickets and own the code changes.
ashley: Do we need customer comms? Any evidence of customer data exfil? So far looks like only metadata access attempt, no PII. My recommendation: SOC/internal only; no external disclosure.
maria: Filing post-incident writeup. Owners: samir (code fixes), jon (network/infra), kevin (token rotation & KMS), ashley (runbook update). Target: 48h for initial remediation.
incidents-bot: Status: mitigations applied (egress block, CDN purge, key rotation in progress, host-header validation rollout). Incident closed to monitoring. close_ts: 1849001180.
devops-bot: Deploy note: host-header validation v1.2 promoted as canary (10%) -> 100% over 30m. deploy_id: dep-7789.
ashley: Runbook update pushed: steps for immediate egress block, KMS key rotation guide, log queries to find affected previews, and detection rule: `alert when preview-proxy requests internal IPs > 5/min`.
kevin: Also flagged long-lived SSH certs used by preview infra for rotation. Creating ticket SEC-2301 to integrate certs into KMS-backed keystore.
samir: I'll draft a short blameless postmortem and schedule a 30m retro for 16:00 UTC today. Adding follow-ups: add unit/e2e tests to ensure proxy rejects internal targets, add eval to Redwood Optimize to flag regressions.
ashley: Thanks all — monitoring until next 24h then update stakeholders.
